# Write compatibility corpus

DOCX files that Raffica Write opens, saves and (from Task 11 on) lays out, with the manifest that says where each file comes from. The file `corpus.json` lists every file; the tool `bench/write-corpus` checks it and runs the round trip. The files are real-world documents from permissively licensed test suites plus the generated thesis; nothing here is made by Word unless the manifest says so.

## Layout

```
testdata/write-corpus/
  corpus.json            the manifest (schema 1)
  README.md              this file
  licenses/<source>/      the licence text (and NOTICE) of each public source; own files point at the repo LICENSE copy
  <id>/<id>.docx         one folder per file (later also word.pdf, word-accept.pdf, word-reject.pdf)
```

An entry of `corpus.json` has `id`, `path` (relative to the corpus root, forward slashes), `sha256`, `source` (URL or text), `license` (SPDX id), `licenseFile` (relative to the root), `retrieved` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `features` (tags).

## Licence rule

Allowed: `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `CC0-1.0`, `CC-BY-4.0`, and `GPL-3.0-or-later` for files generated by this project. Every file carries its source URL, licence, retrieval date and SHA-256 in the manifest and its licence text in `licenses/`. A file whose licence cannot be established is not committed: read the repository's licence and check that its test-data folder carries no other licence or restriction before taking a file, and when in doubt leave the file out. Prefer small files (each at most 1 MB, the whole corpus at most 15 MB). The source URL is the exact file at a commit, never a branch.

## Commands

All commands take the corpus root explicitly. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 findings, 2 usage. Output holds root-relative paths only and never document text.

```
dotnet run --project bench/write-corpus -c Release -- check --root testdata/write-corpus
dotnet run --project bench/write-corpus -c Release -- run --root testdata/write-corpus [--out <csv>]
dotnet run --project bench/write-corpus -c Release -- add <docx> --root testdata/write-corpus --id <id> --source <url|text> --license <spdx> --license-file <path>
```

- `check` reports a file that is not in the manifest, an entry without its file, a hash mismatch, a licence outside the list or without a licence file, a `features` tag the detector does not find in the file, a required feature that no file covers, and a missing `source` or `retrieved`. `--allow-uncovered` leaves out the uncovered required features (for a work-in-progress corpus; CI does not use it, so a required feature without a file fails the build).
- `run` opens every file, saves it to a temporary file and prints `id,opens,saves,unloadedIdentical,loadedEquivalent,ms`: parts the model did not load must be byte-identical, parts it loaded must be equivalent (the rule of the save tests). Exit 1 when any entry fails; an entry that is not a package reports `opens` false and the others still run.
- `add` copies the file to `<id>/<id>.docx` (or `.docm`), copies the licence text to `licenses/`, computes the hash, detects the features and appends the entry. It refuses an id that exists and a licence outside the list.

## Sources

| Source | Licence | Files | Licence text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| generated: `spikes/write/testdoc`, seed 4242 | GPL-3.0-or-later | `thesis` | `licenses/thesis-LICENSE` (the repository LICENSE) |
| Apache POI, `test-data/document`, commit `e0658769cb7f` | Apache-2.0 | ids `poi-*` | `licenses/apache-poi/LICENSE` and `NOTICE` (the `legal` folder of the repository) |
| generated: `DocxBuilder.RightToLeft` (`tests/Raffica.Write.Tests/Support`) | GPL-3.0-or-later | `generated-rtl` | `licenses/thesis-LICENSE` (the repository LICENSE) |
| Open XML SDK, `test/DocumentFormat.OpenXml.Tests.Assets/assets/TestDataStorage`, commit `431ab05cf160` | MIT | `oxml-sdk-equation` | `licenses/open-xml-sdk/LICENSE` |

### Licence stance

- For the kept Apache POI and Open XML SDK files the licence is the **repository's**. Neither repository states a licence per file and no exception for the test-data folders was found. The provenance of text inside a document was not independently verified.
- Files whose content evidently derives from third-party sources (Wikipedia excerpts, news sites, web downloads) are excluded. Removed after review, with the reason: `poi-delins` (hyperlinks to Wikipedia, probably excerpted text), `poi-drawing` (links to a news site, embeds an OLE object), `poi-bib-chernigovka` (the file name is a download from a third-party website), `poi-rtl` (Arabic Wikipedia links), `poi-word-with-attachments` (Wikipedia links in three languages, five embedded OLE parts).
- `generated-rtl` replaces the RTL coverage: built by `DocxBuilder.RightToLeft` with short greetings written for it (Hebrew and Arabic, `w:bidi` paragraphs, `w:rtl` runs, a bidi table). `GeneratedCorpusFileTests` checks the builder; to write the file again run that class with `RAFFICA_WRITE_RTL=<path>` and add the result with `write-corpus add`.
- `sections`, `toc` and `rtl-text` come from our own generated files only (`thesis`, `generated-rtl`), `equations` rests on the single file `oxml-sdk-equation`, and `comments`, `hyperlinks` and `tracked-changes` rest on one real file each (`poi-comment`, `poi-test-document`, `poi-tika-792`); Word-made specimens are to be added in milestone 4.2.
- `poi-60316` has an external `attachedTemplate` relationship (a local file path); nothing ever fetches it.

## Adding a file

1. Check the licence (rule above). Download the file into its own new folder; it is untrusted data and is opened by nothing but `add`.
2. `dotnet run --project bench/write-corpus -c Release -- add <docx> --root testdata/write-corpus --id <id> --source <raw URL at a commit> --license <spdx> --license-file <licence text>`. The tool copies the licence to `licenses/<id>-<name>`; for a source with several files move the text to `licenses/<source>/` once and point `licenseFile` there.
3. Run `check` and `run`, then the tests (`CorpusRoundTripTests`); commit the file, the licence text and `corpus.json` together. Ids are lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

## Feature tags

Required: `paragraphs-runs`, `styles`, `numbering`, `sections`, `tables`, `merged-cells`, `footnotes`, `endnotes`, `fields`, `toc`, `comments`, `tracked-changes`, `pictures-inline`, `pictures-floating`, `text-boxes`, `headers-footers`, `hyperlinks`, `bookmarks`, `content-controls`, `equations`, `rtl-text`. The detector decides each tag from the part XML alone; the table of the rules is in the comment of `bench/write-corpus/FeatureDetector.cs`.

## Word PDFs

The reference PDFs (`word.pdf` and the accept/reject variants) are made by the owner in Word on Windows; the steps are added with the layout comparison (Task 12).
